newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares seen stabilising in coming weeks.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares seen stabilising in coming weeks.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares were active and slightly firmer on Wednesday, with brokers predicting the key industrial index was set to stabilise following a three-week long losing run.
"We saw some big volumes traded today and I think the market is now stabilising," said one broker.
"We're expecting a number of (corporate) results tomorrow (Thursday) and a number of them should be good so I can see confidence returning to the market," he added.
Brokers said most institutional investors had been waiting on the sidelines for company results before taking their positions on the market.
Other buyers had deserted the bourse in recent weeks for the local money market were firming interest rates promised higher returns on investments.

The industrial index put on 2.93 points on Wednesday to close at 10,031.18. Counters to gain were clothing retailers Edgars, 15 cents up at 710 and cement producer Porthold which put on 20 cents to 1,670. Other shares traded within 10 cents of their previous levels.
Minings were largely inactive and the seven-share index there closed unchanged at 1,015.49.
